llm1_reasoning: The conjecture directly asserts NEXP ⊆ P/poly, which by Karp-Lipton theorem implies PH collapses to Σ₂. This collapse is considered highly unlikely, triggering the barrier. The implication is direct and unavoidable under standard complexity assumptions.
llm2_reasoning: The conjecture directly asserts NEXP ⊆ P/poly, which by Karp-Lipton implies PH collapses to Σ₂. This collapse is considered a major barrier because it contradicts the widely believed assumption that PH does not collapse. The conjecture's truth would thus trigger the barrier via this implied collapse.

conjecture.title: Every NEXP language has polynomial-size circuits
conjecture.statement: For every L ∈ NEXP, there exists a family of circuits {C_n} of size poly(n) deciding L.
